facts.fact: Ethiopia's presentation to an APAI-CRVS meeting in July 2026 lists birth registration and certificate and death registration and certificate among the vital services of the national eCRVS (Civil & Family Registration System), alongside marriage, divorce and adoption.
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

facts.fact: The presentation describes the national eCRVS as a homegrown, decentralised, multi-tenant system on a shared digital architecture in which city administrations and regions provide all services, and lists limited accessibility in offline mode, rural connectivity, power and too few tablets as gaps; it does not describe the record-making step at an office in more detail.
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

facts.fact: The presentation sets out a phased rollout: Phase 1 a pilot in Addis Ababa, Phase 2 scale-up to Amharic-speaking regions, Phase 3 national expansion to non-Amharic-speaking regions; it gives no count of offices using the system and does not say which phase had been reached by July 2026.
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

facts.fact: The presentation, given by an Ethiopian official, calls the eCRVS a homegrown system built for ownership and reduced dependency, driven by the Prime Minister's Office and done under the Prime Minister's leadership; it names no vendor or partner as operator.
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

facts.fact: The presentation states a phase-based implementation and national rollout plan for the eCRVS (pilot in Addis Ababa, scale-up to Amharic-speaking regions, national expansion), tied to the 2030 Digital Ethiopia vision; it gives no cost or dates for the phases.
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

facts.fact: The presentation states no source of finance for the eCRVS, domestic or donor (July 2026).
facts.system: National eCRVS system (Civil & Family Registration System)

systems.owner: not named in the presentation; initiative driven by the Prime Minister's Office
systems.tiers: city administrations and regions provide all services; pilot in Addis Ababa, then Amharic-speaking regions, then national

systems.system: Health facility birth and death notification (eCRVS user role)
eCRVS integration with National ID and payment systems
